decision.what: Data the page does not fully understand renders anyway, above an amber banner naming what was not recognised. A missing content block is the only fatal case and reaches the existing error panel.
decision.why: User's explicit choice. A hard refusal would let a future engine release take the live page down; payroll seeing the figures it can plus a loud warning beats a blank error box.

decision.what: data/exports/hours_export_<ingest-time>_covers-to-<last-work-date>.csv, with a seconds-resolution fallback if the minute-level name exists.
decision.why: The old name was the last work date alone, so two exports taken weeks apart collided whenever no new days had been added — and the documented fix, --force-export, overwrote the earlier file. The archive is the audit trail; an archive that can be overwritten cannot answer "which export did this figure come from".

decision.what: The copy to website/public/web_data.json sits in regen.sh, not ingest.sh.
decision.why: regen.sh is what produces web_data.json, so anyone running it directly also keeps the site in step. ingest.sh calls regen.sh and inherits the behaviour for free.

decision.what: regen.sh builds into web_data.json.tmp and renames it into place only after the integrity checks pass; a trap removes the temporary file on any exit.
decision.why: It previously wrote the real file then validated, so a rejected run left the working tree holding refused data with the engine's copy and the website's copy disagreeing until someone ran git checkout. Turns "bad data never reaches the published file" into "never reaches either file".

decision.what: CumulativeChart plots hours rather than minutes.
decision.why: Chart.js picks tick positions round in whatever unit it is given. Minutes produced 33.33 h / 66.67 h; rounding only the label gave 33 h / 67 h, still not round. Plotting hours gives 0/50/…/300 h. The numeric conversion lives in format.ts (minutesToHoursValue) so the cardinal rule holds.

decision.what: ingest.sh does the work; ingest-check.sh wraps it and reports PASS/FAIL on five things afterwards. Both kept.
decision.why: A human wants the report and the next command; the eventual update.sh on a timer wants a plain exit code. The wrapper's real value is catching silent failures — notably that regen.sh only prints a NOTE and exits 0 if website/public is missing, so a run can look successful while the published copy is stale.

warnings.warning: THIS SNAPSHOT SPANS TWO ERAS. The conversation that produced it did its work on 2026-07-28/29; the repo then moved on in a session on 2026-08-10 that this conversation did not participate in. Everything under current_state was read from the files today and is accurate; but do not assume the 2026-07-29 pipeline work is the frontier — schema 1.2.0 is.

The container's HOME is /home/filipejunqueira/containers/claude-home, NOT /home/filipejunqueira. So `~/.local/bin` from inside a session does not resolve to the user's real ~/.local/bin where nhs-log-ingest and nhs-log-deploy live. Always use the absolute /home/filipejunqueira/... path when touching the user's own dotfiles or PATH.
`rm -rf` is denied by the user's global settings, with no exceptions — an allow rule cannot override a deny. Build a fresh directory rather than clearing one, or use `rm -f` on single files.

Interactive aliases bite in Bash tool calls: `cp` is aliased to `cp -i` (it will silently prompt and NOT copy — use `command cp -f`), and `ls` is aliased to lsd (which rejects flags like --time-style — use `command ls`).

`pkill -f "some pattern"` matches the shell running your own command line, because the pattern appears in it. It will kill your own tool call. Use a pattern that cannot match itself, or stop background tasks another way.
The Bash working directory resets to the repo root between calls. Every command that depends on being inside website/ or a sandbox must `cd` explicitly in the same command.

The shellcheck PostToolUse hook blocks a .sh write on ANY finding, including a genuinely half-finished edit (it caught `target` referenced but no longer assigned during this session). A rejected write is that hook working, not a tool fault — read the output and finish the change.

engine_v2/ is deny-listed for the Edit and Write tools, but that does not stop a script from writing inside it at runtime — regen.sh writes engine_v2/web_data.json every run. Running regen.sh or ingest.sh for a check therefore dirties the working tree with a new `generated_at`; revert with `git checkout --` if the content is otherwise identical, so the data files do not churn.
